originalText.text: I just discovered this spot today, and let me tell you, I walked in thinking, alright, it looks good, but does it taste good? Well… the answer is YES. Yes, it does! First up, the fried whiteys. Crispy, fresh, seasoned just right — I almost had to look around and make sure my momma, grandma wasn’t in the kitchen. Then came the collard greens. Now, listen… not everybody knows how to make collards. Some cook them without flavor  and put a lot of sugar. But THESE? These tasted like real-deal, Southern, know-what-you’re-doing collards. Then came the mac and cheese, and Lord have mercy. I took one bite and suddenly I was stomping my feet and doing the hallelujah dance right in the kitchen. It brought me straight back to my late mother’s food, specifically her MAC & CHEESE. It was rich, creamy, and cheesy to perfection. The candy yams were sweet buttery happiness in every bite. By the time I finished, I had already sent pictures to my family telling them, “Y’all need to try them out.” Annette and Arthur — y’all know EXACTLY what you’re doing in that kitchen. Honestly, if I could hire you both and tie y’all up in my kitchen to cook for me every day, I would! Next week, I’m coming back for the potato salad and banana pudding, because if they’re anything like what I had today… whew, I might not leave. This place brought me nothing but happiness, happiness, happiness. Y’all must check them out! They’re the TRUTH!!!

originalText.text:
Disrespectful, careless, and zero accountability
Do NOT order takeout or delivery from this place. Matter of fact, don’t dine in either if you value respect.

I placed a delivery order, spent $40, and even tipped the delivery guy, just to receive the wrong rice, missing items (my mojito never showed up), and a whole lot of attitude. When I called calmly to explain the mistake, instead of fixing it like professionals, I was met with rudeness and disrespect.

I politely asked if they could bring the correct rice and the missing condiments. The guy flat-out refused, then had the nerve to hang up the phone on me while I was trying to resolve an issue THEY caused. That tells me everything I need to know.

Places that treat customers like that cook with no love, no pride, and no care. If you can’t own your mistakes or speak to people with basic human decency, you shouldn’t be in the food business.

Save your money, save your appetite, and save your peace.
Plenty of Dominican spots in the Bronx that actually respect their customers. This is not one of them.

I recently ate here and the experience was nothing short of delightful. The warm ambiance and rustic decor created a welcoming atmosphere. The staff was friendly and attentive, providing excellent service throughout the meal.

Now, let’s talk about the star of the show—the Spanish chicken. The menu boasted a variety of flavorful dishes, each showcasing the chef’s expertise in combining traditional Spanish flavors with a modern twist. The chicken was perfectly cooked, tender on the inside with a crispy, golden exterior that left my taste buds dancing.

The appetizers were equally impressive, with options ranging from patatas bravas to chorizo croquettes. Each bite was a burst of Spanish authenticity. The chef’s commitment to using high-quality ingredients was evident, enhancing the overall dining experience.

The drink menu featured a well-curated selection of Spanish wines and cocktails that complemented the meal superbly. The sangria, in particular, was a refreshing choice that added to the festive atmosphere of the restaurant.

What truly stood out was the attention to detail in presentation. Each dish was a work of art on the plate, showcasing the chef’s dedication to not only taste but also aesthetics.

As for the dessert, the churros were a delightful way to end the meal. Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and accompanied by rich chocolate dipping sauce—a sweet ending to a savory journey.

In summary, this Spanish chicken restaurant exceeded my expectations. From the inviting ambiance to the delectable dishes, every aspect of the dining experience was carefully crafted. I highly recommend this establishment to anyone seeking an authentic taste of Spain with a modern flair. ¡Delicioso!

I hosted a senior luncheon at Dallas BBQ on June 26, 2026, and the experience was absolutely amazing! The food was outstanding. The baby back ribs were incredibly juicy, tender, and meaty, and the Dallas BBQ sauce is simply to die for. It was so delicious that many of us ordered more food to take home. I only wish I could have taken a whole bottle of that BBQ sauce with me!
Our server, Eva, was exceptional. She was attentive, friendly, professional, and made sure everyone in our large group was well taken care of from beginning to end. In all my years of dining out, I can honestly say she is one of the best servers I've ever had. Dallas BBQ is fortunate to have her, and I truly believe she would make an excellent Server Coordinator, helping train and mentor other staff.
I also want to recognize the manager, Connie, who was welcoming, professional, and made sure everything ran smoothly. Between the outstanding food and the exceptional customer service, I have absolutely no complaints.
Thank you, Dallas BBQ, Eva, and Connie, for making our senior luncheon such a wonderful experience. We will definitely be back for more of those delicious baby back ribs—and hopefully another taste of that unforgettable BBQ sauce!

This is one of my top Dominican restaurants in the entire city.  Everything on the menu is good.  What I really love are the special dishes on specific days.

One day I picked up here and saw the selection, it looked delicious.  I tried the mangu and loved it.  It was seasoned and had a consistent texture.

Whatever I pair it with is perfect.  Be it steak, pernil, bacaloa, etc.   All the meats are perfectly seasoned and tender.

Finally, what really won me over was the homemade hot sauce they have.  One day I finally put it on my pepper steak and mangu, I’ve been hooked since.

I’ve tried everything from the ribs to the oxtail and the goat. This is quality food, a hidden treasure.  I’m glad I found it.

I was highly surprised to find this new soul food/caribbean fusion self-serve restaurant on my way home. It’s a very tight spot with all the food selections lining the side and rear walls. They have an array of beverages available and although only have banana pudding as a dessert option, are working on expanding their dessert selections.

There are signs asking that customers put gloves on and not talk over the food. Food is weighed by the pound, a little pricey for the residents in the community but most likely optimized for the large hospital presence in the area. I tried the Mac n cheese, fried chicken, collards and yams. The chicken was fried and seasoned well, the  collards were tasty, not overly seasoned yams had a slightly heavy clove taste and as beautiful as the Mac n cheese was presented there was a buttery taste to them.

So overall it was ok, and it’s definitely the only eatery of its kind in the area so it will definitely gain momentum as word spreads. I will go back and try their other options before determining if they would be a go-to option for me when I’m in the area.

originalText.text:
Black consumer beware! I know ppl have been going to this restaurant for as long as it’s been around, but the community really needs to reconsider. I went in after not going for some time, (literally more than a year+ - and only by invitation by my mother) and I was reminded why I NEVER GO IN HERE. I asked for the chicken with rice and beans. This used to just be a simple lunch special type order. You would have thought I asked for mountains to be moved and for heaven to be brought down to earth. The server, one who apparently spoke no English, I guess put the wrong type of rice because when I said I want beans, she got the nastiest attitude and asked if I wanted a side order of beans. I said no. I just want the beans that come with my meal. Chicken. Rice. Beans. I didn’t understand the problem. But then, it became clear. She was supposed to add the white rice. And becasue she didn’t, she was not going to give me beans. Like, what?!? She proceeds to speak in Spanish and speak to another server there to very obviously complain and curse me out. The other server was actually apologetic to me, but clearly couldn’t control the first one. I wasn’t even upset until the first server continued to act like I was  inconveniencing her because she needed to change the rice. Lady, just put the beans on the rice! There were literally two Spanish people that ordered before me and one - a Puerto Rican friend of mine from the neighborhood ORDERED THE SAME THING, and there was no issue. No rudeness. When she was serving me, everything changed. I absolutely should have walked out as she carried on too afraid to speak English or just not able to.  I did not walk out because I had already come from across the street where the food looked a bit dry. I just wanted to have a a quick delicious Spanish style lunch. While the one server was nice enough, I just said this is the second time at this location that I have been treated like this and I think it’s because I am black and I don’t speak Spanish. My mother always goes there, but she absolutely looks Puerto Rican so she never has an issue, but I am BLACK! Very BLACK! I will NEVER PATRONIZE THIS PLACE AGAIN. MY (OUR) PRESENCE AND MONEY IS NOT VALUED! I was standing at the counter paying for my food and the server was STILL being horrible. For the life of me, I can’t understand why black folks continuously patronize businesses by other cultures that would NEVER patronize theirs. I NEVER SEE ASIAN OR HISPANIC OR INDIAN PPL IN ANY BLACK OR AFRICAN BUSINESS. I’ve been very good about avoiding certain businesses and I cook a lot at home. But every now and again I just want to dip my toe back out to test the waters. I get bitten every time. Lesson Learned. PS. The food was NOT EVEN GOOD. And I’m not saying that to be petty. It was NOT GOOD. SMH. Chicken dry, beans bland. I had to add my own Goya beans when I got home.

Edit: Do yourself a favor and read through the lowest ratings. I read after posting and ppl have been experiencing this and other terrible things for years. Nothing has changed. And then do yourself another favor and avoid if you are black (unless you speak Spanish).

Staff member openly coughed multiple times over the food prep station, then wiped his nose with his hand. I complained that I was concerned about his unsanitary and unprofessional behavior as I was waiting for my food, and asked to speak to the manager. He then claimed he was the manager, told me to leave, and threatened to call the police.
Note that a quick search online with NYS Health Department for Rocbody shows multiple food violations, including: " Wiping cloths dirty, not stored properly in sanitizing solutions; Non food contact surfaces of equipment not clean; Floors, walls, ceilings, not smooth, properly constructed, in disrepair, dirty surfaces; Lighting and ventilation inadequate, fixtures not shielded, dirty ventilation hoods, ductwork, filters, exhaust fans".
I will never support this business again, nor do I recommend that anyone else does, for their own safety. Not to mention how completely disrespectful and unacceptable that behavior was from a supposed manager of a food service establishment.

Unfortunately, it was not very practical to eat. The onion layers kept falling apart, so it was almost impossible to hold like a normal burger.

Everything tasted good and the prices are very reasonable. Definitely will be returning back.

originalText.text:
Jeez. Where do I begin about this place.

Jeez, where do I even start about this place? 8-Bit Bites is probably the number one burger spot in New York City. I don't know who decided to start this concept that has become a very popular place, but I'm so grateful that this place exists because where else can you get, you know, just unhealthy food that we used to eat as kids and teenagers and even adults still. I'm still an adult kid, right? And be able to play retro video games. I mean, this is just heaven. If I could sleep here, I probably would. To go over the food, I would rate it 5 out of 5 only because of all the options that are available. Some of the french fries and tater tots can use a little bit more seasoning, but their seasoning is very delicious and it's not overpowering to the palate. It can also be a little pricey, so just make sure when you come here to eat that you're very hungry because you don't want to come and then you have food left over that you paid a lot of money for. There's a lot of video games here. They have all of the retro systems. I mean, even systems I never played as a kid, so there goes that. Overall, it was a great experience, at least at this location. I'm pretty sure the other ones are also just as well. The employees are all very nice. Usually the managers, especially the one that works here, is very professional. I always see him here. He's always providing advice on how to play the video games and how to work the systems. They provide seasoning here, printing services. You can order online. The delivery is usually really, really fast. Overall, it's just a super accommodating fast food joint. What can I say? It would take a lot for somebody or another chain to top what 8 Bit Bites has done, so I hope they continue to expand.

Food is acceptable, though I detect some BS in their menu and marketing.

Staff seems preoccupied with everything else accept helping customers.

The machine failed to print my receipt and when I asked one staff member for help she acknowledged my request then ignored me. The other staff member gave me the "GRILL SLIP" and said here's your receipt. When I explained that it is not a receipt she explained the price of the item to me. I mentioned that the receipt machine needs to be repaired and she didn't know how to respond. I also noticed that the receipt machine was separate from the actual ordering screen menu and so I was able to open the receipt machine without any tools (there's a small lever that you push to release the entire receipt paper roll).

Overall the atmosphere was immaculate and quiet for a Thursday morning at 11:29:19am however I feel their interior design and ergonomic layout could use some improvements. I also noticed the staff packaging "TO GO" meals and using regular packaging tape to seal the tops of paper bags, not small stickers like Wendy's or McDonald's. This was a huge red flag and a sign of inconvenience.

In addition, I found that there were numerous members of staff, sitting, walking, talking, idling, and twiddling their thumbs, not doing a damn thing. Perhaps it was because they were patiently awaiting the lunch hour rush. IDK and IDC but it appears to the untrained eye that Bojangles is in the business of wasting time and money.

Lastly, I enjoyed the sandwich in the blistering hot sun which I found quite delicious.

originalText.text:
Today, our visit to Bojangles was a mixed experience. We spent around $31, and my daughter enjoyed her three-piece tenders, which were flavorful with a pleasant hint of spice. Unfortunately, whole chicken wasn’t available at the time. I sampled the peach cobbler and the biscuit with steak, adding gravy on the side. However, the gravy was disappointingly thin and lacked flavor, and the steak resembled more of a processed patty than a real cut of meat—leaving much to be desired in taste. On a brighter note, the coleslaw was exceptionally good, while the mac and cheese was just average.

The trip itself was fine until we arrived. The staff member directing traffic was efficient and did an excellent job managing the flow, though his approach came across as somewhat forceful. I was impressed to see the manager and regional manager on site offering him support and encouragement, especially after what seemed like a difficult previous day. Their positive attitude truly helped make the best of the situation.

A few suggestions came to mind during our visit: the employees working outside should be provided with something to keep them warm. Additionally, it might be worth considering moving to online-only orders—such as through Uber or a drive-thru system—since some individuals inside appeared to be lingering without ordering, which can slow down service for those waiting to order and go.

Finally, when school lets out, the restaurant tends to get overcrowded with students. For safety and efficiency, it could be helpful to have some form of security or crowd control in place. Perhaps implementing a one-way entry and exit system by closing one gate would help manage the flow and maintain a more orderly environment.

If you’re looking for a fresh take on Haitian cuisine in Brooklyn, BunNan is absolutely worth a visit. Their creative plantain forward menu puts a unique spin on traditional Haitian flavors, and it delivers.

We had the griot served in crispy plantain cups, and they were nothing short of outstanding. The pork was tender, well-seasoned, and packed with authentic flavor, while the crispy plantain cups added the perfect sweet and savory crunch. It was the ideal light appetizer and a great introduction to the meal.

BunNan does an excellent job of honoring Haitian cuisine while presenting it in a modern, creative way. If this appetizer is any indication of the quality coming from the kitchen, we’ll definitely be back to explore more of the menu. A must-visit for anyone looking to experience Haitian food with a fresh twist.

1 Star — Extremely Disappointing Experience

This was by far the worst Burger King experience I’ve ever had. I visit Burger King locations quite often, but this particular location was unbelievably disappointing.

First, I waited almost 20 minutes for my order, even though there weren’t many customers inside. There was absolutely no reason for such a long wait.

During that time, the employees were arguing and talking among themselves, sometimes laughing and joking while customers were standing there waiting for their food. There were around four employees working, but instead of focusing on preparing and handing out orders efficiently, they were just walking back and forth without any sense of urgency.

The cashier also spent nearly 20 minutes dealing with one customer, while other customers were left waiting.

When I finally received my food, the disappointment continued. The fries portion was extremely small — you can clearly see it in the photo. The burger was completely cold, which made me feel like it had been prepared a long time ago and simply left sitting somewhere before being handed to me.

On top of that, the dining area was very dirty and poorly maintained.

I honestly don’t understand how a location with several employees can provide such slow and careless service when there weren’t even that many customers.

I will never come back to this Burger King again.

Worst Burger King experience I’ve ever had. Very disappointing.

One critique I could give is that whoever puts the order together doesn't pay close attention to what goes on the burger. I put down I didn't want tomatoes, but alas there were tomatoes on the burger. I also requested to dine in and they didn't give me a tray for my food. Not really too big of a deal, but the staff needs to be a bit more mindful on getting orders correctly. Overall, the food was decent, even though I do prefer McDonald's fries.

The staff here was pleasant enough as I didn't see any issues. I also saw staff wiping down tables that were used, so I don't understand other reviewers stating otherwise.

There is plenty of onsite parking and they do drive thru orders. The prices here are standard and not too crazy for a meal. All in all I would stop in again in the future and give this place another shot.

Tldr; wonderful Cantonese food spot that exceeds expection in taste, quality, and price point. Come here, highly recommended.

My mom learned about this place from her Chinese WeChat friend group (so you know it's good when it's spread via words of mouth by the Chinese community, low key I should gate keep this but I'm not going to!). We had a huge dish of Singapore noodle, double lobster, pork congee, and added on this huge dish of clams all for under $100. They are all tasty, fresh, and you can tell the chef is experienced from big restaurants bc it has that kind of quality. The price point is so down to earth, mom says this is the neighborhoods canteen during lunch hour so maybe avoid peak then when you come. The servers mostly speak Toisanese. But I see foreigner customers so they must also serve in English. It's not a glamorous spot, but it's a underrated neighborhood spot that deserve all the respect. Will definitely be back! They also serve dim sum!!

The roti canai came with curry chicken/potato, and it was so flaky and yummy, just how it should be! The sushi was also good (we got spicy tuna). If I could give this place more than five stars, I absolutely would. Highly recommended to anyone looking for great food, fresh juices, beautiful vibes, and genuine hospitality.

originalText.text:
After moving away from Brooklyn nine years ago, I finally made my way back to Dallas BBQ, and let me tell you, it was everything I remembered and more.

The food was exactly how I’ve been craving it all these years, amazing flavor, great quality, and that same signature taste that no one else can replicate. I always go for the sticky tenders, and there is truly nowhere else that sells anything even close to them. They’re unmatched! The price as well was amazing! It feels good to be able to go out and not have to spend your life saving just for lunch!

The drinks were just as good as I remembered, strong, flavorful, and actually worth the money. You’re not just paying for an overpriced slushie, you can genuinely taste (and feel 😅) the alcohol. Every sip was worth it.

Our waiter was incredibly kind and attentive. He kept checking in on us, made sure every request was handled with care, and even surprised us with dessert. Not once did I feel like I was being a bother, he made us feel so welcomed. That kind of service makes all the difference.

The photographer walking around was such a nice touch too. I ended up buying a cartoon version of my family, and it honestly brought so much joy to the day. I felt like a tourist in my own old neighborhood.

If I had one small suggestion, it would be to update the carpet. It’s been there since I can remember, and it has developed a bit of an old odor. But once the food and service came, I was able to fully enjoy the experience.

With the quality of the food and the amazing service, this place can truly stay a hit forever. So happy I came back, it felt like coming home.

originalText.text: I've been coming here since I was a kid and have had many great lunchtime memories with my family here. It was also our go to anytime my parents didn't feel like cooking. I remember always getting the fried fish with tofu over rice, which I haven't had in a while so I definitely need to come in again and try that. On this most recent visit, we ordered some stir-fried lobster (for takeout - from the looks of it, it doesn't look like they're currently doing indoor dining anyway) and it was served in a tray, as opposed to those white cardboard containers. It was perfectly stir fried with morsels of ground meat, egg, and of course black bean. I'm glad they're still around and that we have a consistently good Chinese restaurant to go to.

I called the location and asked to speak with a manager but was told that no manager was available. I then explained what I had witnessed, and the employee responded that sometimes it gets hot, so employees take their shoes off. This is not an acceptable explanation for serving food without proper footwear.

I hope management takes this matter seriously and ensures employees are following appropriate health and sanitation standards. The Department of Health has also been notified regarding this concern.

Brooklyn’s Best Zabiha Halal Spot – Gyro King on Coney Island Ave 👑

If you’re looking for authentic halal food in Brooklyn, look no further than Gyro King (984 Coney Island Ave). This place is a game-changer for anyone craving late-night halal platters, gyros, and chicken tikka, and it’s proudly 100% Zabiha Halal (Hand Slaughtered) with HFSAA certification for peace of mind.

What I ordered & loved:
•	Chicken Tikka Platter – smoky, juicy, and cooked to perfection, with fluffy rice that soaks up all the flavor.
•	Lamb Gyro with Rice – tender shaved lamb packed into a generous portion, balanced with salad, pickles, and their signature sauces.
•	Mixed Grill Combo – lamb chops and chicken tikka together on one plate. Absolute fire.
•	Family Combo Platter – huge, shareable, and perfect for anyone who wants to try a bit of everything.

The white sauce and hot sauce are the secret weapons—creamy and spicy in just the right balance. The portions are massive, the prices are more than fair, and the service is quick even when the line wraps around.

What sets Gyro King Coney Island Ave apart is the Zabiha Halal integrity. In Brooklyn, a lot of places advertise halal, but these guys are hand-slaughtered, verified, and consistent, which makes all the difference in flavor and trust.

Bottom line: This isn’t just another halal counter—it’s one of the best halal restaurants in Brooklyn. If you’re anywhere near Flatbush or Coney Island Ave, make the trip. It’s open late, it’s certified, and it’s guaranteed to hit the spot. 🌙🔥

I fondly remember this place from prepamdemic. It was a great spot to get inexpensive, good cantonese roast meats.
The food variety now remains with my favorites of noodles and rice and your options of roast meats. They recently expanded their opening hours into the later night so people can enjoy after work, too. The prices are still pretty decent compared to how expensive and problematic quality for roast meats can be. But their portions do feel smaller now.
At night, there's not a lot of people but also not a lot of stock left. However, they seem to always have enough for that late night bowl of noodles to just satisfy a craving. Now that it's a snowy and chilly time, that is even more welcome.
The ownership has changed from when it used to be King's Kitchen, and service is a bit more sparse. However, the waitress I had was very attentive and friendly. I'm glad to see this place open into the night again and I hope they do well.

Jam’It Bistro is the kind of neighborhood Caribbean spot that quietly overdelivers. The jerk chicken came out glossy, smoky, and properly charred, with that sticky sweet heat that keeps building bite after bite. Juicy all the way through, especially the dark meat, with rice and peas underneath soaking up every drop of sauce.

The curry goat was the comfort-food standout — deeply seasoned, rich, and slow-cooked until tender, with a thick curry gravy that tasted like it had been simmering for hours. The cabbage on the side balanced everything out perfectly and kept the plate from feeling too heavy.
No fancy plating, no gimmicks — just authentic Jamaican flavors done right. One of those meals where you instantly know the kitchen cooks from experience, not shortcuts. Brooklyn comfort food at its best.

Unfortunately, the posted business hours are not reliable. The employees state “9am” and the hours posted on their door state they open at “9am”, but I arrived at 9:08 AM and the door was still closed. This a constant reoccurring issue. A worker inside saw me and another customer waiting but did not acknowledge us until I knocked and pointed to the porridge. They also do not answer the phone, making it difficult to know when service is actually available.

Once served, the portions were inconsistent. The other customer’s porridge was filled to the second marked line/triangle, while mine was noticeably below it. When I politely asked for a little more to bring it to the same level, I was told no because it was supposed to be filled to the line.

My concern is the overall inconsistency in hours, communication, and customer service. Very disappointing. I would like to support this local business, but these experiences make it very difficult to do so.

I'll definitely be coming back for more. If you're in the area and craving authentic Jamaican patties, this is the place to go!

I was bummed to get a message from my delivery driver that Jamaican Flavors did not have bone-in jerk chicken ready, but they did have boneless. I was very annoyed, but very hungry, so I begrudgingly accepted the revised order and I'm glad I did.
Boneless Jerk chicken w/macaroni and cheese- what a generous portion! But aside from that, flavor! Jumped in my mouth, spice level was perfect that I could even enjoy with my toddler. Seems they use chicken thighs which is a huge boost to flavor! And the Mac and cheese was gooey and they did not skimp on cheese (see my video clip of the cheese pull!). Had to take this down in 2 sittings.
Spicy beef patty- this is what I was jonzin for. Great amount of filling, not greasy, meat was still moist, spice level was super enjoyable with a little bit of a longer, light burn.  Spice is meant to flavor, not to hurt. Pastry shell was lightly crispy. Size was lager than most.
Spicy beef patty w/ Jamaican cheese-
Curiosity order here. I have no idea what Jamaican cheese is, but it tastes great! I did enjoy this more than I did American cheese. My only feedback is that I wish the cheese was distributed better in the patty.
Ordered a Jamaican juice- slammin! I don't know what it was. But I think it was orange ginger and carrot. I was super pleased that there was no ice, just a cup full of fresh juice. Absolutely worth the value and order.

The kitchen was kind enough to double my patty orders, I'd imagine to say "sorry we couldn't give you exactly what you ordered" and the gesture is appreciated. That's hospitality. Even though I wasn't there in person, they wanted to take care of me. I will order from here again.

I've been to this restaurant maybe a total of about five times within the past two years. Prior to this I saw no reason to give a review, today I walked 4.5 blocks from work and back. I purchased a (mini) curry goat meal that cost $10.89. That would be considered a small size at most other places. To start If you want a filling and flavorful meal for about $5-$6 more, just bypass this place. I would've rather gone to stand on a line, at CJ Jamaican restaurant nearby (time didn't permit).

There seems to be a shortage of other good quality eateries in the area. The server asked me if I wanted gravy with the rice and peas. I said yes and then looking at the entree, it looked tasty! When I proceeded to open it and started eating, I stumbled upon enough bones to make me choke or cut my gums. Whoever hired her a younger girl with nice teeth, needs to have a talk with her. Any ensuing injury would've been grounds for a lawsuit. The gravy wasn't enough and there was a lack of spicy taste or (pepper) in it.

In my careful assessment of Caribbean cuisine, I'd rate 🇹🇹 top notch, next is 🇬🇾 then the rest of the pack, maybe Jamaica gets 3rd place. J'ca is a proud culture however, they ought to do a little better overall. Trini spots tend to always have a line, especially in Brooklyn since they're scarce in number.

originalText.text: It’s so refreshing when you try a black / Caribbean owned restaurant and have no complaints. The guy that served me was super nice and friendly. The restaurant was extremely clean. It’s a mix of Guyanese, Jamaican and Trinidadian. The menu is extensive but not overwhelming. So many great options, I couldn’t decide on one thing so I decided to try an Ackee patty, a lunch special meal which consisted of rice and peas, fried chickens and cabbage and a shark burger with sweet potato fries. EVERYTHING was amazing. There was a bit of a wait for the shark burger as they make it fresh to order which I can appreciate. My sister had the lunch special and as you can see by the photo, she thoroughly enjoyed her meal. I can’t wait to return to try their smoothies and wraps and bowls. I wish they were in my neighborhood but I’ll be back :)

This was a steak, egg & cheese bagel with a large sweet tea, and honestly… this visit surprised the hell out of me.

The biggest difference was the customer service. It felt more like Europe than the U.S. — calm, respectful, no rushing, no attitude. My host was on point from start to finish. Not sure if it’s the morning staff, but whatever they’re doing works. This did not feel like the McDonald’s we grew up with in the 90s. Different energy. Better standards.

The food was fresh and hot, the bagel was done right, and the sweet tea was cold and refreshing. One noticeable change — the sandwiches are smaller now. And honestly? I’m not mad about it. Americans could use better portion control anyway. Quality over excess. Boom.

No complaints.
No nonsense.
Just a solid experience done right.

5 stars, easy. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
I’ll be back.

Without the Kpop Demon Hunters and Super Mario Galaxy collaborations, I would’ve given this place one star. The quality and service here are honestly disappointing.

I rarely come to this McDonald’s, but I made an exception for those collaborations. I placed a “to go” order at the kiosk, but no receipt was printed, so I had to rely on memory for what I ordered.

The experience only went downhill from there. One of the female staff members who handled my order had a very poor attitude from the start. My drinks came out first, but there were no straws, so I had to ask for them. Not a huge issue, but it’s basic attention to detail.

While waiting for my Super Mario Happy Meal, I noticed the same staff member holding it and staring at the screen in the back for several minutes. When she finally turned around, she looked almost surprised and handed it to me without saying anything—no apology, no acknowledgment of the delay.

When I asked about my two burgers, she took the Happy Meal back without explaining anything, opened the box, and showed me that the burgers were inside, then handed it back to me without even closing it. The interaction felt dismissive and unprofessional.

The final issue was when I asked for a paper bag for my “to go” order—something that should’ve been included in the first place. She rolled her eyes and gave me attitude just for asking.

For the quality of the food and the service I received, it was not worth almost $30. The only positives were the Kpop Demon Hunters cards and the Super Mario Galaxy toy, which were the main reason I came in the first place.

Overall, this experience was frustrating and disappointing. There’s a huge lack of basic service and organization. I really hope management takes this seriously and works on improving both staff behavior and overall customer experience.

⭐☆☆☆☆

I come to this McDonald’s almost every single day just to pick up my coffee, and unfortunately the experience is consistently frustrating.

Most mornings the place is basically empty, yet I’m left standing at the counter for 2–3 minutes with no acknowledgment. The employees clearly see me, but no one makes eye contact or asks if I need help. I often hear the staff in the back chatting and gossiping in Spanish. I’m Spanish myself, so that’s not the issue — the issue is being ignored as a customer while my order is already paid for and sitting there. It completely defeats the purpose of ordering pickup.

When I finally do ask for help, the attitude is usually unpleasant. There is one specific young employee (thin, with braids) who consistently has a very nasty attitude. You can say “good morning” or greet her politely and she looks visibly annoyed, as if being spoken to is a problem. I understand she’s young and still learning, and I would never want someone to lose their job — but customer service clearly isn’t the right role for her right now. She needs better training or to be placed elsewhere.

I’ve lived in this neighborhood for over 20 years. I’ve had my own ups and downs and understand bad days happen, but this is an every-day issue here. A little acknowledgment, professionalism, and basic courtesy would go a long way, especially for regular customers.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously, because this location could do better.

Located on the busy stretch of Broadway in Brooklyn, this McDonald’s serves as a convenient stop for a quick meal, whether you’re on the go or looking for a familiar bite in the neighborhood. Like most McDonald's locations, it offers the full classic menu—burgers, fries, chicken sandwiches, nuggets, and of course, the iconic Big Mac.
The food here is exactly what you’d expect from the global chain: consistent, fast, and comforting. The fries are usually hot and crispy, and the burgers are made to standard. During peak hours, the freshness can vary slightly depending on how busy the kitchen is, but overall, the food meets McDonald's usual quality.
This location also offers breakfast items, which are surprisingly satisfying—especially the Egg McMuffin and hash browns. If you're looking for something sweet, the McFlurry or apple pie is always a nice treat.
As for service, the staff is generally efficient and polite, though lines can get long during lunch hours. There are self-service kiosks available, which make ordering faster, especially if you’re customizing your meal.
The dining area is simple but functional. It’s usually clean, with enough seating for small groups and individuals. . Like many fast-food spots in NYcy it can get a little crowded or noisy, particularly after    school hours or late    evenings.
Overall, this McDonald’s does its job well. It’s not a gourmet experience—.    but if you’re in the area and craving classic fast food, this location delivers exactly what you need: quick, familiar, and affordable eats

My husband and I ordered here twice already last month and today and both times the food was delicious. The meals are made to order and they taste fresh and all are a decent amount of food per meal for the price it’s a great deal. A great place to get fresh delicious food with flavor. My daughter loves the jerk flavor it had a kick she’s a spicy lover and I got the mango sauce I honestly can’t get enough my 2 year old daughter shared with me and she licked her fingers. My husband is from Spain he knows good seafood when he has it and he loved everything. We got shrimp which was cooked to perfection the muscles they had absolutely no sand which you can know by that if they clean the seafood. I have not one complaint.

The first time we ordered we picked it up since it was late and they were closing soon and my husband got to meet with one of the owners they had a wonderful conversation as he finished up with our food and packed it up. He stood late to cook all our food which we appreciated.

The owners are great people, today we meet the other owner as he delivered our food both very respectful gentleman. They cook and care for you like your family! Can’t recommend eating from here enough whether dining in or out the food is worth it and if you’re there you got great company to talk to while you wait for your food.

I had such as incredible, unexpected experience.  I am in the hospitality industry and very picky about service. I was searching for some good seafood from traveling from Long Island to Brooklyn to visit my in-laws for Mother's Day. I read the reviews and saw the photos.

There was a technical glitch and the owner reached out to inform me and was not supposed to be working but took time out of his schedule to drive out to the restaurant to prepare my order.  He was friendly, warm and provided exceptional service.

Once you walk into the restaurant, your mouth will water up. When we ate the food, it was well seasoned to perfection. Absolutely delicious and it is a must have for all seafood lovers. We also got fried chicken. My in-laws were looking for me. Don't forget to stop by for your order.

This was my first visit to Pepas. First let me start by saying the staff was friendly and welcoming however the kiosk to order the food with a credit card wasn’t working properly and took much longer then it would have been had we just been able to order with a human.

The food itself was by far the worst Jamaican food I’ve had to date. We ordered the jerk chicken and “jerk” was far from what it was. There was absolutely no flavor in the chicken and it was extremely dry. Little to no seasoning. It tasted more like dry grilled chicken at best. We also ordered the jerk pork which was terrible. The pork again had no flavor and really just tasted like boiled pork. I watched them scoop the pork out of a liquid broth so I knew right then it wasn’t grilled. I’ve been to Jamaica before and jerk pork should be made on the grill with a ton of seasoning when done properly.

Here are a few photos I took when I got home.

I frequent this Popeyes locations fairly often, and they never let me down in terms of quality and freshness.  The quality of the food has always been good and never disappointing. What really stands out is the professional and excellent customer service provided by Umar (works the front counter taking orders and packing orders at the same time), not just for me, but also any and all patrons I witness coming and going while I'm waiting on an order.  Umar is always courteous, professional, and efficient in what he does.  He's always on top of his orders, whether it be in person or an online/mobile order making sure everything is in check, and whether the kitchen is on top of pushing out whatever is needed to fulfill an order.  Always friendly, courteous, and professional with a smile.  Takes orders, prepares, and pushes orders out as fast as humanly possible without any discrepancies.  Occasionally, there might be something out of stock which was ordered ahead of time off the app, but Umar will always make every reasonable effort to make things right.  Location has also always been clean and tidy.  Overall, definitely would recommend this Popeyes location due to their cleanliness, quality of food, and the excellent service provided by Umar and his team.

- John -

originalText.text:
There’s a particular kind of hunger that hits you on Brighton Beach Avenue. Not the romantic kind. Not the “let’s explore something new” kind. The kind that says: give me something fried, familiar, and fast before I make a bad decision.

So I walked into Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen.

Now, Popeyes—on its good days—is a beautiful thing. Crunch, grease, salt, regret. All the essentials. But this… this was not one of those days.

The room felt off the second I stepped in. Not gritty in a charming, lived-in way. More like something had quietly given up. Two guys were out cold at the front tables, which in New York is less shocking than it should be, but still sets a tone. Not exactly the kind of energy you want when you’re about to trust someone with your lunch.

I ordered a three-piece. Simple. Foolproof. Or so I thought.

Ten minutes later—ten long, echoing minutes in an empty fast-food joint—my tray arrived. The chicken? Fine. Hot, crispy, doing the bare minimum to uphold the brand’s reputation. No complaints there.

But then you hit the sides.

The mashed potatoes were ice cold. Not room temperature. Not “sat out too long.” Cold like they’d been thinking about winter. And the gravy? Imagine someone describing gravy to you over the phone who’s never actually tasted it. Watery, confused, completely devoid of purpose. It wasn’t offensive. It was worse—it was indifferent.

Then came the biscuit. Hard enough to qualify as sporting equipment. I half expected it to bounce. If it had “Property of the NY Rangers” stamped on it, I wouldn’t have questioned it.

This is the kind of place that reminds you a franchise is only as good as the people running it that day. And on this day, whoever was in charge checked out long before those two guys at the front tables.

You walk in expecting comfort food. You walk out wondering what exactly went wrong—and how something so simple got so thoroughly botched.

I had one of the worst customer service experiences at this Popeyes location. We approached the counter/window and showed the young lady the promotion that was advertised for $20 with the option of either 11 tenders or 9 wings. I simply showed her the picture and said I wanted that deal. At no point did she ask whether I wanted tenders or wings, so she automatically put in wings.

When we later asked for sauces, we were told we would be charged 50 cents per sauce. I explained that sauces normally come with tenders, and that’s when the confusion started. Instead of trying to resolve the misunderstanding professionally, the employee became argumentative and kept insisting that we ordered wings.

Another employee, who appeared to be some type of supervisor or person in charge, got involved and made the situation even worse. I calmly tried explaining what happened, but he only wanted to hear himself speak and showed no interest in helping or understanding the issue. I then asked to speak to a manager, and instead of getting one, he rudely called someone on the phone who never came out or spoke to me.

The employee then said, “Since I’m not dealing with this, I can give you a refund.” At that point, I accepted the refund because the entire interaction had already become frustrating and disrespectful. When I asked for his name, he refused multiple times and then eventually gave me what seemed like a fake name, which I found extremely insulting and unprofessional.

I did not appreciate the way we were treated as paying customers. The lack of communication, poor attitude, and disrespectful behavior completely ruined the experience. Customer service goes a long way, and this location seriously needs improvement in how they handle guests and resolve simple misunderstandings.
Ps this is the person that made everything so horrible and was extremely unprofessional I do not recommend this place if this person is working there!!!!

Original review:
Proper Popeyes taste and beautiful looking restaurant right in the heart of Greenpoint...but very sub-par for a grand opening.

The Good:
Food tasted great and was what I expected.
Beautiful interior, very clean (as expected for opening day).
Conveniently located at Greenpoint Ave /Manhattan Ave.

The Bad:
No warm welcome or smiles. Now.. I don't always expect this from a fast food joint, but for a grand opening, I did expect at least a luke warm welcoming. What good is a balloon arch without a smile?

They did not have ANY jam for the biscuits.
I cried a little.
They also didn't have the sauce I'd chosen, displayed at the register (wild honey). I wasn't given an alternative for the sauce so I used my own at home when I realized I had 8 nuggets and 0 sauce. I was offered honey for the biscuit. I feel as though the jams are a staple of Popeyes Biscuits 🤷🏾‍♂️

Staff were a bit chaotic behind the counter, and the cashiers seemed to fumble a bit at the register. It's day one, and I believe it was my cashiers first day on the job so I give that a pass; but perhaps they opened too soon/not enough training? I'll chalk it up to stress, but again I felt that stress as the customer which was the opposite of what I expected walking in.

Three of the soda flavors were out at the fountain, with little "out" notes taped to them.

I wasn't given a spork for my red beans and rice. Or napkins. I actually wasn't even given a Popeyes paper bag for my to go order, it was a plastic bag (see photo).

Overall:
I'll definitely stop by again because I'm a fan of Popeyes, but man what a bummer. I was really excited to get in there on day one to take great photos and leave a glowing review. I think in a week or two they'll have their legs under them and hopefully it'll be at least the average Popeyes experience.. complete with advertised condiments, jams, and at least Popeyes branded bags.

If you guys see this, please do better! I love Popeyes, and just want a nice experience in your restaurant.

Original review:
Proper Popeyes taste and beautiful looking restaurant right in the heart of Greenpoint...but very sub-par for a grand opening.

The Good:
Food tasted great and was what I expected.
Beautiful interior, very clean (as expected for opening day).
Conveniently located at Greenpoint Ave /Manhattan Ave.

The Bad:
No warm welcome or smiles. Now.. I don't always expect this from a fast food joint, but for a grand opening, I did expect at least a luke warm welcoming. What good is a balloon arch without a smile?

They did not have ANY jam for the biscuits.
I cried a little.
They also didn't have the sauce I'd chosen, displayed at the register (wild honey). I wasn't given an alternative for the sauce so I used my own at home when I realized I had 8 nuggets and 0 sauce. I was offered honey for the biscuit. I feel as though the jams are a staple of Popeyes Biscuits 🤷🏾‍♂️

Staff were a bit chaotic behind the counter, and the cashiers seemed to fumble a bit at the register. It's day one, and I believe it was my cashiers first day on the job so I give that a pass; but perhaps they opened too soon/not enough training? I'll chalk it up to stress, but again I felt that stress as the customer which was the opposite of what I expected walking in.

Three of the soda flavors were out at the fountain, with little "out" notes taped to them.

I wasn't given a spork for my red beans and rice. Or napkins. I actually wasn't even given a Popeyes paper bag for my to go order, it was a plastic bag (see photo).

Overall:
I'll definitely stop by again because I'm a fan of Popeyes, but man what a bummer. I was really excited to get in there on day one to take great photos and leave a glowing review. I think in a week or two they'll have their legs under them and hopefully it'll be at least the average Popeyes experience.. complete with advertised condiments, jams, and at least Popeyes branded bags.

If you guys see this, please do better! I love Popeyes, and just want a nice experience in your restaurant.

I recently visited Sheep by Barashka in Brooklyn and really enjoyed the experience. It has a cozy, slightly “home-style” atmosphere with Caucasian/Russian cuisine — very hearty food, generous portions, and you can genuinely feel that everything is made with care.

The dishes were mostly great: the grilled meats were juicy and flavorful, the salads felt fresh, and the hot appetizers and meat dishes stood out the most. It’s a great spot for both a family dinner or a casual night out with friends — relaxed, warm, and unpretentious.

The atmosphere deserves a mention as well — nice interior, sometimes live music, and overall it feels like a comforting, traditional gathering space.

The only small downside is that service can occasionally be a bit slow, but it doesn’t really ruin the overall experience.

Overall, it’s definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for filling, tasty food and a cozy, welcoming vibe in Brooklyn.

Found this place while looking for Umi Sushi & Seafood Buffet in google. The one we went to was in Hillside Ave over at Queens, but I wanted to go to a place that was essentially closest to my home.

That's when I discovered Umi Premium Sushi & Seafood Buffet over by Nostrand Ave. When I looked through the pictures with my friend, I stated the place looked really nice. I even caught my eye on the tree by the entrance. There was an even bigger display of food to choose from, and y'know I had to grab myself some. So I told my parents about this place and they have agreed trying out the buffet.

Our reaction? Phenomenal. We were satisfied with the service. All the employees that we've met have been so nice throughout the buffet. My family enjoyed it all. Even my brother John Copeland (the one who recently made a review) was really happy on joining us for dinner last time.

We visited so much that most of the people that work in the buffet knows me and my family. Especially one in particular that always say hi to me. Even though at times I couldn't say Hi back cause I was shy, but I was happy to see that I was being recognized.

I love their lobster, I always go to the sushi section cause I really love sushi. And whenever I want to go out and eat, I'd always come to eat here. It is so nice!

Overall, I say 10/10 on everything. Keep up the good work! Love the food, the employees, good atmosphere, it has it all. Despite the parking lot though. I think that's fine granted that this place is nearby Fun Land and Aldi. I also didn't know this place use to have a party city. Oh well

originalText.text:
Very disappointing experience. We drove about an hour to come here for dinner and were both really excited because the restaurant looks beautiful from the outside. Unfortunately, once we sat down, the experience was completely different.

Dinner for two came out to over $100, and for that price I expected much better quality, cleanliness, and service. The staff was not friendly or welcoming, but the biggest problem was the food. It was honestly so bad that I couldn’t finish my meal. The lobster smelled extremely unpleasant, did not seem fresh at all, and tasted even worse. I actually started getting a stomach ache while I was eating.

Nothing we tried tasted fresh. The desserts were terrible and didn’t even look appetizing, and the fruit was also very disappointing.

To make things worse, the bathrooms were dirty and there wasn’t even soap available to wash your hands. For a restaurant serving food, that was especially concerning and made the overall experience even more unpleasant.

For the amount of money we spent and the hour-long drive to get there, this was absolutely not worth it. We went in excited to have a nice dinner together and left extremely disappointed. Based on our experience, I would not come back or recommend this restaurant.

The Crispy Pork Belly / BBQ PIG / Siu Yuk (烧肉) had crispy skin, an acceptable taste, it was a bit greasy but it's what gives it the most flavor 😂 The Roast Pork / Char Siu (叉烧) was soft and delicious, very good taste. originalText.text:
A cool concept, but unfortunately not worth the price.

This is a really cool idea and would be a  great place to stop by with friends, if the prices and food were better.
Sticking with their "Eat like a kid again" theme, part of doing out as a kid was getting a solid burger and fries for 5$. That's no longer the case.

Now I get that they have extra costs to cover, paying for the TVs and game consoles and whatnot, but the food really isn't worth the price.

I paid $24 for this meal, and it really wasn't a good deal. The burger was tiny and thin. It tasted ok for a fast food burger, but it really wasn't enough food and left me unsatisfied and feeling a bit ripped off.

Either lower the prices or provide a better meal and I'll consider coming again, but until then unfortunately it's not worth it. Can get more food for half the price at McDonalds or another burger joint.

Stopped in here for a late night bite after a show at Irving Plaza before the long drive home back upstate.
The customer service was great. A few of the controllers connected to the emulators seem to have seen some better days(which is expected with excessive use), but overall a really cool spot to hang out late at night.
We ordered two smoothies, a breakfast sandwich and a double smash burger.
The smoothies were delicious, and both sandwiches were also very good.
To top it all off, on the way back to the car, my girlfriend dropped her smoothie and I ended up going back to get a replacement, fully expecting to have to pay again, and it was on the house.
Really made my night before the long drive back home. Would definitely stop in here again for a quick bite.

Great Food, Fast Service, and Perfect Times Square Location ⭐🍗🗽

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I had a great experience at Dallas BBQ in Times Square, New York City! 🍗🗽

The location is perfect for anyone who wants to enjoy the famous Times Square vibe. It is very close to Times Square and right in front of Madame Tussauds NYC. The restaurant is large, with two big floors and a third level with more than 10 tables. Even with that size, it is very popular, and you can see from the photos that almost every table is filled. 👏

The food was excellent. The steak was amazing and cooked very well. The sticky wings, Hennessy Wings, BBQ sauce, yellow rice, baked potato, and cornbread were all very good. The portions are large, and the prices are affordable for the location. The margaritas were also great. 🍹🥩🍚

Seating was quick, and the service was very good and fast. The waiters were friendly and helpful. The floors and restrooms were clean, which made the experience even better. 👍

This is one of the best restaurants if you want to invite friends, and I have done that many times before. If you are coming with a group, it is better to reserve a table ahead of time. 🍽️

Just keep in mind that drink refills are not free. Also, the tip is added automatically to the final bill. In my experience, it was about 7%, which is fair. They also give you the option to leave an extra tip if you want.

Overall, Dallas BBQ Times Square is a great place for food, service, location, and value. I highly recommend it! ⭐️🍗🗽

originalText.text:
The Dallas BBQ Chelsea restaurant in Chelsea offers very good value for money.
If you go during peak hours, be prepared to wait around 15–20 minutes, as it is extremely popular and usually very crowded.
You can try many classic American specialties there, including ribs, chicken wings, and of course the usual frozen piña coladas and various mixed alcoholic drinks. Alcohol is very expensive — at least as expensive as the food itself.
The food is not fine dining or high-end cuisine, but one thing European visitors should definitely keep in mind is that the portion sizes are completely different from European standards. Everything is enormous. Therefore, when ordering, it is worth considering ordering less if you do not want food to go to waste, because the portions they serve are so huge that it is almost impossible to finish them.
Overall, it was a good experience. It is a very loud place where everyone speaks loudly, so do not expect a calm, quiet restaurant where you can have an intimate conversation with your partner. The clientele is generally more casual and less elegantly dressed.
That said, as I mentioned, the food is very good, the atmosphere is lively and enjoyable, and overall I can definitely recommend it.

I don’t usually leave negative reviews, but I felt this experience call for one.
I’ve been coming here for a long time for a quick meal and have spent a considerable amount of money over the years. The food is decent, and I mainly come because it’s convenient in the area.

On this visit, 7/05/2026, I place an order of goat (chivo). I watched the new, short Dominican employee put only 3? small pieces of meat for a $14 plate. I wanted to say something but decided to let it go.
I also ordered a side dish of salmon & asked for the price before ordering. The employee told me it was $7. After I paid, about 3  minutes later, the short one came back and asked me for an additional $1. When I asked why, she said, “The price went up.”?????
The price went up in the 3 minutes after I paid? WONDERS!

I asked to speak with the manager, but another employee simply told me that “next time it will be $8.” I responded that there wouldn’t be a next time because this was poor customer service and changing prices after a customer has already paid is misleading and unacceptable.

Instead of addressing my concern professionally, the short employee made a comment about me being rude. Customers should not be made to feel like they’re the problem for questioning inconsistent pricing.
I won’t be returning. Be cautious when ordering here, and always confirm your price before paying. Based on my experience, the pricing appears inconsistent, and the customer service  especially the new short object leaves much to be desired.

Warm, friendly Cantonese spot with genuinely attentive service and an unassuming, welcoming vibe. The menu is broad and classic — roast meats over rice, noodle soups, fried dumplings, and all the typical Cantonese comfort dishes.

I tried the soup noodles, which were decent, and I’m looking forward to coming back to try more of the menu. Prices are transparent (cash v car) and good value.

I also liked that the restaurant is tucked off the main road, giving it a more local feel. There’s a surprisingly spacious seating area around the corner, making it easy to sit down and enjoy your meal. Locals and tourists both seem to like this place, and I can see why.

A solid, affordable find — I’ll be back to explore more dishes.

originalText.text:
Cruel, Bizarre, and Completely Disrespectful – Avoid This Location

I have eaten at McDonald’s locations all over the world my entire life, and I have never been treated with such blatant disrespect and hostility as I was at this location. If I could give zero stars, I would.
I stopped in on July 4th during the middle of a massive heat wave. Desperately needing some water, I made a point to be a paying customer and ordered food and a beverage first. When I received my order and politely asked the server, Ruben, for a cup of water, the nightmare started.
* The "Hot Water" Incident: Ruben made a bizarre, disgusted face at my simple request. He then deliberately handed me a cup of hot tap water—again, during a dangerous summer heat wave. It tasted completely off, so I politely asked for regular, cold water.
* The Silent Treatment: He proceeded to completely ignore me as if I didn't exist. When I patiently waited at the counter, his attitude shifted from dismissive to outright hostile.
* The "Manager" Excuse: He bizarrely claimed that giving a customer water required "manager approval"—an absurd policy I have never encountered at any McDonald's globally. He went to speak to someone, came back, said absolutely nothing to me, and went back to ignoring my presence.
* The Unhinged Climax: When I finally asked him again, he flat-out refused to give me water. Frustrated, I explained that the main reason I bought a meal was just to get some water in the heat. In a completely spiteful and unjustified response, Ruben said, "Does that mean you don’t need this drink?" and literally snatched my paid drink away from me.
This wasn't just bad service; it was cruel, petty, and deeply hurtful. Over a simple cup of water.
Management needs to seriously evaluate who they are putting behind the counter, because Ruben’s behavior is a massive liability to this franchise's reputation. Do not go to this location unless you want to be actively bullied by the staff. Absolute worst customer service of my entire life.

I visited this location during my first trip to New York, hoping to use up some loose change and have a simple order. A small tea with hot water and a tea bag. I placed my order at the kiosk, intending to pay in cash, but I wasn’t familiar with how to use the cash machine. So I went to the counter to ask for help and pay directly.
I waited at the front for about 10 minutes, trying not to be a bother, as the cashier seemed busy and not very approachable. When I finally asked for assistance, I was told to go to the machine in the back. I explained that I was having difficulty and just wanted to pay cash for my order (I had the exact amount, $1.62), but instead of helping, she pointed to the work behind her and said she had too much to do.
I completely understand that fast food environments can be busy and demanding. I wasn’t expecting exceptional service, but I was honestly surprised by how dismissive the interaction felt. A little guidance or basic courtesy would have made a big difference.
To be honest, the experience left me feeling so unwelcome that I couldn’t help but think it might have been better to just toss my $1.62 into a fountain and make a wish instead.
As a first-time visitor to New York, this was quite disappointing.

originalText.text:
⭐⭐

Disappointing customer service experience

I visited this McDonald’s today around 6 PM after leaving my doctor’s office to meet my mom at her job. While I was on my way, I urgently needed to use the restroom.

I approached the security guard and first tried speaking Spanish, thinking he understood. When I realized he didn’t, I asked him in English if I could use the restroom. He told me I needed to make a purchase. I understand that McDonald’s may have a restroom policy, and I had no intention of refusing to purchase something. I simply needed to use the bathroom urgently and was trying to explain that.

What upset me was the way I felt dismissed. I understand security concerns, but there is still a way to speak to customers with basic courtesy and empathy. I ended up purchasing a Coca-Cola just to use the restroom, but I was so bothered by the interaction that I left the drink behind.

I later spoke with the manager on site because I wanted to express my concern about how the situation was handled. However, the manager was also very dismissive and seemed to give me the runaround when I asked for the security guard’s name. She acted as though she did not know who he was or what his name was. That was very concerning to me because it is difficult to believe that employees at McDonald’s would not know the name of the individual hired to provide security at their location.

I continued explaining to the manager how uncomfortable and upset the interaction had made me feel, but I did not feel heard or taken seriously. Her response made the situation even more frustrating. It left me wondering whether this has happened to other customers and whether this is how guests are treated at this McDonald’s.

I also couldn’t help but wonder whether someone who was pregnant or experiencing another urgent situation would have been treated differently.

I’m not asking McDonald’s to ignore its policies. I’m asking that employees, especially those interacting directly with customers, be reminded that how you speak to someone matters. A little understanding and decency can make a big difference.

I enjoy McDonald’s, which is why this experience was so disappointing. I hope management takes this feedback seriously, reviews what happened, and addresses both the security guard’s conduct and the manager’s dismissive response.

As for the restaurant itself, I can’t complain about the atmosphere. It was pleasant, with nice background music, and everything looked clean.

My only issue was the food. It didn’t have the quality or the signature taste that I usually expect from McDonald’s. I’ve had McDonald’s fries in many countries around the world, and the fries at this location didn’t taste like the classic McDonald’s fries at all.

The burger was also disappointing. It looked squashed, the bun was very small, and the beef patty reminded me of the thin breakfast sausage rather than a regular McDonald’s burger. Overall, it lacked the familiar flavor that keeps me coming back to McDonald’s.

I hope this was just an isolated experience, because I normally enjoy the consistency and quality that McDonald’s is known for.

Headed to the kiosk and bought the cheapest thing I could find to giveaway to someone in our car which was an extra small soda.  Golden ticket (or white thermal paper) in-hand, I was allowed through the pearly gates to pee.

I was deciding whether or not to even pick up my order but did so anyway.  Child on the receiving end was happy and so was I.

Came into this location with the intention of buying something small and using the restroom as a paying patron (like a normal person would). I ordered at the kiosk without issue. I looked on the receipt for the bathroom code, I didn’t see it. I walked to the labeled bathroom next to the counter and tried the handle, locked. I asked the lady at the counter for the code, she said it’s at the bottom of the receipt. I tried the code several times and it didn’t work. Then the keypad locked out.

I asked the employee hey can you open the bathroom, the code doesn’t seem to be working. She said I need to go upstairs. I asked, is this bathroom not working, she said it works but I have to go upstairs. I said, why can’t you just open this one? I have heavy bags and a disability. She said it’s for employees only. Clearly one can see it is not labeled as such. She said I can leave my bag here at the counter. Not ideal, but sure. I tried to place my bag behind the counter and another employee stopped me. I said this lady said I can put my bag behind there. She said no, it would have to be in the corner, in the public accessed area. I said you must be crazy to think I’m going to leave my bag out for anyone to take.

So I struggled up the stairs to use the bathroom. I had to leave my bags upstairs to grab my food. I checked the bag to make sure it was accurate. Took out a fry to try, it was cold and stale. I asked for fresh fries, she gave me a look and rolled her eyes to ask another employee for another medium fry and placed it in the bag. This one, while warmer in temperature, was also lacking in taste and was not evenly crispy. I went back upstairs to my bags to try to enjoy my meal.

The spicy McCrispy was very messily made. Had sauce all on the outside of the bun, lettuce falling out in the box. Looked in the bag for napkins, none in the bag. No stations upstairs for napkins, straws, condiments, nothing. Back downstairs I went to ask for napkins and condiments, to be greeted with an unenthused employee again.

I’m not expecting 5 star service at McDonald’s, but basic etiquette and customer service should be the bare minimum. I understand some locations are havens for the unhoused population, but some measures and practices need to be reevaluated on a basic human and customer level.

This place is amazing! As soon as you enter, there are so many different Asian places to order from, with so much variety. I ended up going with a stand called Bei Fang and ordered the stir-fried noodles with beef (I asked for extra spice). I also went to the dim sum stand and ordered some custard buns, and might I say, both dishes did not disappoint.

The noodles had a good amount of spice, and the beef was nice and tender, not chewy at all. The custard buns were warm and fluffy with a creamy filling, and they weren’t too sweet, which I really liked.

The only downside was that it was really hot inside while I was eating, which made it a little uncomfortable. However, I did go on the hottest day of the year, so I understand that probably played a role.

Despite that though, I will definitely be coming back to try more of the different food options they have!

Despite that though, I will definitely be coming back to try more of the different food options they have!

The employee even told the officers he still wasn’t going to honor the order. One of the officers took my phone, verified my receipt, promotion, and order details, compared everything with the store’s records, and explained to the employee that my order was legitimate. Only after the police intervened did he finally give me my food.
No customer should ever have to involve the police just to receive a paid order that both Uber Support and the officers confirmed was valid. I will never return and would not recommend ever!!!😡😤

originalText.text:
I think this is one of the worst Popeyes locations I’ve ever visited. The atmosphere is extremely unpleasant, mainly because the restaurant is constantly crowded with delivery drivers occupying nearly all the tables while not even eating. Whether it’s hot or cold outside, customers who actually want to sit and eat often have no place to sit.

The food itself is acceptable, but the chicken quality is inconsistent. Quite often it contains a lot of sinew and feels poorly prepared.

However, the biggest issue by far is the staff of the store. Communication is extremely difficult, as many employees struggle to speak basic English, and even simple questions or orders often lead to confusion. The ordering system seems to overwhelm the staff completely, and even after placing an order, employees repeatedly ask to see the receipt because they appear unable to locate or understand the order in the system. Especially the Indian lady seems not fitting at all.

Overall, the service experience is chaotic and frustrating. This location seriously needs better management, improved staff training, and a complete overhaul of customer service standards.

So disappointed with my experience at N & M Pizzeria. My family and I have been customers for years, either dining in or ordering delivery. While we've had a few minor issues in the past, nothing compares to what happened tonight.

I ordered a large cheese pie and three drinks. Unfortunately, the only items worth having were the drinks. The pizza arrived completely burnt, hard, and practically inedible. The crust and slices were so overcooked that eating it felt like it could break a tooth.

I called to let them know about the issue, and to their credit, they apologized and offered to send a replacement pie. However, if a pizza in that condition made it out the door the first time, it raises concerns about quality control. I didn't feel confident accepting another one.

This was a very disappointing experience from a place we've supported for years. Based on this experience, I won't be ordering from here again.

Carribean Taste Budz (nearby on Sutphin blvd) lunch special packs more chicken in their lunch special size than a large order from Blaze 718 that is far tastier AND cheaper and all around more authentic.

Likely won't try again given that every part of my order (jerk chicken, rice,  plantain) was bland and hardly worth eating. Sad excuse for jerk chicken. You're better off walking up the block for legit Jamaican beef patties from Carribean Delight for less half the price than ordering from this spot.

THANK YOU MANAGER: KAJAL

Drive - thru order.

I ordered the $5 special, $6 special and $6.99 Buffalo wing special. ALL great value.

I got home and noticed my buffalo wings didn’t have any buffalo powder on it and the $6 2 piece spicy fried chicken special was over cooked and hard.

I called back and received amazing great customer service from the manager. She was very polite and said no problem just come back and I will fix it.  When I got there she couldn’t find my order in the system. I showed her my receipt. When I showed her on my phone the number I called she then called my number. I had called the wrong location in at Hempstead. We both laughed. I had called the wrong location both had gotten my order from Manager Kajal’s location on Union Tpke.

She said no problem I will dis it. Go ahead and pull up and I will bring it to you. Just a few minutes later she was back.

I’m in a wheelchair in a car with hubby so she didn’t have to go the extra mile to bring it to us.

Manager Kajal replaced both orders and gave me a couple extra fried chicken at no cost which she didn’t have to and of course I never asked. It was all hot, juicy, crispy and delicious.

She was extremely nice, friendly and wasn’t annoyed or frustrated one bit. Even fast food restaurants give GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE not just regular restaurants.

THANK YOU MANAGER KAJAL ONCE AGAIN.

May Allah bless your business and everyone working here. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic, homestyle Bangladeshi food.

originalText.text: Stopped by Evelia’s Tamales and was seriously impressed. You can tell right away this place is about authentic, no-frills Mexican food done right. I tried a few different things tamales (obviously), tacos, and a quesadilla and everything tasted fresh and flavorful. The tamales were moist and packed with filling, not dry at all. The tacos had great seasoning, fresh cilantro and onion, and that squeeze of lime just brought everything together. Even the drink (horchata) hit the spot. The inside is casual and colorful, with that neighborhood spot energy. Nothing fancy, just good food and solid portions for the price. If you’re in Flushing and craving real Mexican food, this is definitely worth the stop.

originalText.text:
Consistently solid Shanghainese restaurant in Flushing -- definitely one of my favourites in the area, and it's never too busy or pricey (probably cos it's a bit further away from the "main" central area of downtown Flushing).

If you order above a certain amount (I think $30), you can get a free order of the soup dumplings 鮮肉小籠包 (or get free validated parking?). They are really delicious and definitely one of the highlights of this restaurant! They are just practically overflowing with so much soup, with really thin skins and such fragrant, juicy pork fillings.

Some other must-tries:

- Chilli oil wontons 紅油抄手 were fantastic. Portion size was a little larger than I expected, and the chilli oil smelled so good!

- Scallion pancake with beef 蔥油餅夾牛肉 is one of my favourites. The wrapper was very crispy and the beef was tender and very savoury. The balance of the slightly-sharp scallion flavour was perfect.

- Fried chinese chives box 韭菜盒子, another classic. Lovely crispy outside layer with a delicious fresh chives/noodles/etc. filling.

- Soymilks - I've had both the hot and cold sweet soymilks, and they are both delicious. You can't go wrong here.

The location is a bit hidden (in the back of a small mall), which I suspect is why it's not busier. I've never had to wait, even during weekend lunch hours. Service is always very efficient and to-the-point, which I appreciate.

Order a vanilla ice cream and a small hot coffee. You have just made the poor man's affogato.

As you pour the coffee over the vanilla, you stare into the dark swirl. A reflection appears. Is it you?

No.

It's a small old Italian man. He looks at you with quiet satisfaction, gives a slight nod, and vanishes back into the coffee.

For a moment, his memories become yours. Your childhood, our childhood, an Italian childhood. You wonder whether you had been Italian all along.
