originalText.text:
Usually I come to this location at night and everything is fine. The workers are normally sweet and I’ve never really had an issue before, which is why this experience stood out so much.

On Thursday around 7 PM, I went through the drive-thru to get ice cream and cookies. First off, I was already confused because the website/app clearly offers single cookies or smaller cookie options, but this location said they only sell the 3-pack. Whatever, not a huge deal, we bought it anyway.

The issue started at the window. I politely asked the employee if I could get one of the plain black containers from the breakfast trays because we wanted to put the ice cream in it. The employee helping us, Natalie, looked at me like I was speaking another language. She seemed completely confused even after I explained it multiple times. I ended up asking another worker in the back because I genuinely felt like we weren’t understanding each other.

The second worker immediately knew what I was talking about and explained it to Natalie. Instead of just handing it to us, Natalie told us to pull forward and wait. Meanwhile the ice cream is literally melting while we’re sitting there waiting for something that should’ve taken two seconds.

Then on top of that, we had asked for spoons THREE separate times. Once when placing the order, once at the first window, and again at the pickup window. Natalie finally came outside with the container and still forgot the spoons. When we reminded her, she rolled her eyes and said, “Oh my gosh, you should’ve told me before.” Except we literally DID tell you before. Multiple times.

That attitude was unnecessary. I understand people have bad days, but there’s no reason to act annoyed at customers for asking for things that were already requested several times. Especially when every other experience I’ve had here has been good.

This review is specifically because of the customer service from Natalie. Everyone else I’ve interacted with at this location has usually been kind and helpful. Hopefully this was just a one-time thing because if I have another experience like this, I definitely won’t be returning.

We have been to Qing Dao Restaurant a few times. Even though the name sounds like a Qingdao-style restaurant, it feels more like a little bit of everything. They sell breakfast, lunch, cold dishes, cooked dishes, and all kinds of random items. It’s more like a casual place where you can grab something quick when you’re hungry or craving Chinese food.

The food here is not amazing, but it does the job. It is the kind of place where you come when you just want something simple to eat or a small snack to satisfy a craving. We got the pig ears this time, and I was also interested in the beef tripe. I asked if they could do a mixed order, and the lady said yes, but the price would be based on the more expensive item. I honestly have not really heard of that before, since most places usually average the price or make it more reasonable for a mixed order.

Overall, it is okay. Not a place I would come to for really delicious food, but if you just want something quick, casual, and filling, it is fine.

My experiences at Popeyes have been consistently enjoyable, earning it a solid 4-star rating from me. The flavorful menu offerings, particularly the iconic fried chicken, have always hit the spot. The blend of spices and crispy texture is a treat for the taste buds.

The staff is generally friendly and efficient, making the ordering process smooth and hassle-free. I appreciate the convenience of both dine-in and takeout options, especially during busy days.

However, while my visits have generally been positive, there's room for improvement in a couple of areas. Occasionally, the waiting times can be a bit longer, and some items might run out during peak hours. I've also noticed that sometimes the portion sizes can be a bit smaller than expected. Moreover, enhancing the overall dining environment would certainly add to the experience.

All in all, Popeyes remains a go-to spot for satisfying comfort food, and I'll definitely be returning to savor their flavorful offerings again. I hope to see these minor aspects improved in the future.

The food is generally good, though quality can vary depending on the time of day. The atmosphere is simple and casual, more of a neighborhood eatery than a formal dining place.

Overall, it’s a solid option if you’re in the area and looking for a quick, traditional meal.

originalText.text:
This buffet...just isn't it. Definitely can ignore the influencers who keep making a big deal out of this.

Variety is adequate, but quality is severely lacking. Came early for a Christmas day seating when it wasn't too busy yet, and the seafood and meat dishes were not consistently replenished. Shrimp was fine, but lobster and crab weren't cooked well and lacking flavor. Duck was super inconsistent (some good bites, others dry like no other), and even the beef slices, which are difficult to mess up, were difficult to chew. Shout out to the man at the carving station, though: he was attentive, enthusiastic, and incredibly friendly.

Overall, a decent price point, but really not worth it once you factor in the quality.

originalText.text: This is a well-put together hot food section of buffet with authentic flavorful Chinese food and meals . I came for the seafood which I was very impressed with from the salmon, coconut shrimp , jellyfish salad , grilled and stir-fried shrimp, to the yummy clams crab, and other types of fish. There were dim sum as well as yummy stirfried vegetables, fried sweet potatoes ,onion rings ,  and sushi . The fruits for dessert were yummy too . I didn’t care for the cake and ice cream section as those are not healthy /full of dairy. I loved that they have unpasteurized cold-pressed juice for the community but it’s only available for dinner buffet as of now . Hopefully cold pressed juice can be on the menu for lunch buffet . I wish there’s the walnut shrimp dish as advertised ! Despite this, I would go again if someone wants to buffet ! Ambiance is nice and clean too .

Do you like dry egg foo yung?  If so, you are in luck!  This place will gladly spare you the hassle of eating egg foo yung with the sauce that is supposed to come with it!

All so that when you complain that they barely gave you a tablespoon of sauce, they can admonish you for not ordering extra sauce for 50 cents!  "Because it is expensive", they told me.  I said, "Yes, that's why I'm paying you".
Silly me, thinking that I should have at least an ounce of sauce for each egg patty.

Well, if they need the 50 cents, they should just change the price on the menu.  Hasta la vista - beware!

Craving KFC, I decided to indulge myself in their only Tuesdays $10 deal. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a huge mistake and a regret.
The chicken itself was a disaster. Eight pieces of original recipe dark meat were dripping with oil, the breading was soggy, and some parts were even burnt black on the outside. But the worst part was the inside. Several pieces had a disturbingly bloody tinge, completely unappetizing. To top it all off, there was a strange fishy smell to some of the chicken, and a couple of pieces even had an unmistakable odor reminiscent of chicken feces. Needless to say, the entire meal was inedible. This experience completely ruined my KFC craving and left me feeling disgusted. For the price, I expected much, much better. I would strongly advise anyone considering this deal to think twice before wasting their money.

K&P Lounge is off to a rough start. I know it’s day 1, so I can’t be too hard on them, but this was truly not a great first impression. We ordered the shrimp po’ boy (with fries), macaroni and cheese, and the chocolate cake.

- The shrimp in the sandwich was good — fat and flavorful — but the bread was stale.
- The fries were probably the strongest part of the entire meal. They were fine.
- The macaroni and cheese was only macaroni and cheese in the most generous sense of the name — there was pasta and there was cheese, but it seemed like there was no thought put into whether people would want to eat it. The noodles were overcooked and the cheese was congealed as if it had sat in the fridge for a few days and then been reheated in the microwave.
- The chocolate cake was overly sweet, with barely any chocolate flavor. It felt like it was chocolate cake for people who hate chocolate.

We sent the macaroni and chocolate cake back because we disliked them so much. I was personally hungry enough that I didn’t mind the po’ boy, but I would never order it again.

Service was good in spite of all of this.

originalText.text:
I came here on a date and had no expectations whatsoever. The interior is really nice and cozy. It almost feels like you're in someone's home. We were greeted by the waitress at the bar and got to sit wherever we liked. There were two other tables seated as well. We were given menus and water and quickly decided what we wanted to order, but we ended up waiting about 15-20 minutes after getting the menu to actually place our order. Our waitress seemed busy with the other tables. We ordered the Catfish Nuggets and the Jerk Chicken Egg Rolls to start. For entrees my date got Jerk Chicken Pasta with Grilled shrimp, and I got the Po' Boy Sandwich with Jerk Chicken. After we ordered, it took over an hour for us to receive our appetizers. Our waitress wasn't anywhere to be found, and in the moments we saw her briefly, she walked past us without saying a word. No update on our food or anything. We figured that maybe she was busy with the other two tables, but the table beside us had already gotten their entrees, and the other table only had four patrons, so we couldn't understand why it took so long for just the appetizers.

Eventually we got our appetizers and the Jerk Chicken egg rolls looked a bit overcooked. The waitress apologized for the wait upon bringing our food, and even opted to give us an extra Jerk Chicken Egg Roll appetizer to make up for the time waiting. Unfortunately, while my date was a fan of the Egg Rolls, I wasn't a fan at all. I thought the flavor was very light, and there wasn't much spice at all. Figured it was just me. The Catfish Nuggets were superb however, and the sauce they brought with it paired very nicely.

The entrees came soon after we received our appetizers. This is where things get interesting. My date was a big fan of her pasta, but she loved the shrimp. I wasn't a big fan of my Po Boy Sandwich. It was okay but left a lot to be desired. She tried the sandwich and agreed. I thought her pasta was pretty good honestly, and the shrimp was fantastic. The food ove was hit or miss flavor wise. The portions were pretty good considering the price and the area.

Overall, this restaurant is pretty hard to recommend. The service was mediocre at best, and the food was mostly lackluster. Pricing for everything seemed fair overall, but the hour long wait didn't sit well with either of us. I honestly would've given this place two stars, but I gave the additional third star because the waitress did apologize for the wait (without a reason, but hey it's something) and did give us a free appetizer. But even with that, of the four items we ordered, we both only really enjoyed two of them.  Perhaps we'll return to give them a second shot, but I can't recommend this place until I do.
